name: Chocolate brownies
tip: A rich chocolate bake with a crackly top and fudgy centre; cool before cutting for neat squares.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 20 cm square tin with parchment.
Melt the butter with dark chocolate gently; cool for a few minutes.
Whisk sugar and eggs together for 2 minutes, then stir in the melted chocolate.
Fold in flour and cocoa powder, then chocolate chips; avoid overmixing.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the top is set but the centre still has a slight wobble.
Cool fully in the tin before slicing into nine squares. Store chilled if adding a dairy topping.

name: Sticky toffee pudding
tip: Soft date sponge with warm toffee sauce; delicious with vanilla ice cream. Preparation and baking take around 55 minutes.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease a six-portion muffin tin or a small 20 cm baking dish.
Cover the chopped dates with 180 ml boiling water, leave 10 minutes, then stir in the bicarbonate of soda and mash until soft.
Cream 75 g of butter with 100 g of brown sugar; beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour and date mixture.
Spoon into the tin and bake for 25–30 minutes, or until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
For the sauce, gently simmer the remaining 35 g butter, 60 g brown sugar, cream and golden syrup for 3–5 minutes until glossy.
Serve the warm sponge with toffee sauce and ice cream. Refrigerate any dairy leftovers promptly.

name: Lemon drizzle cake
tip: A buttery lemon sponge soaked with citrus syrup and finished with a simple glaze.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Beat softened butter with 160 g caster sugar until pale and fluffy. Add eggs one at a time.
Fold in flour, baking powder and finely grated zest of two lemons; loosen with the milk.
Bake for 45–50 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Warm the juice of two lemons with the remaining 40 g caster sugar; prick the warm loaf and pour over.
When cool, mix icing sugar with enough juice from the third lemon to make a thick drizzle and spoon over the cake.

name: Classic apple crumble
tip: A crunchy oat topping over soft cinnamon apples. Add custard just before serving.
method: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Peel, core and slice the apples.
Toss apples with 40 g sugar and cinnamon in a medium baking dish; add 2 tbsp water.
Rub flour and cold cubed butter together with fingertips until breadcrumb-like, then stir in oats and remaining 90 g sugar.
Scatter the crumble over the fruit without pressing it down.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling at the edges.
Allow 5 minutes to settle; warm the custard separately and serve alongside.
